metadata.summary: MIMIC-IV is a large, freely available database comprising de-identified health-related data associated with over two hundred thousand patients who were admitted to the critical care units and the hospital of the Beth Israel Deaconess Medical Center in Boston, Massachusetts, USA, between 2008 and 2022. The database includes demographics, vital signs, laboratory tests, medications, observations, and notes.
metadata.purpose: To support a wide range of research including early warning systems, risk prediction, causal inference, and interpretability of clinical machine learning models.
funders: National Institute of Biomedical Imaging and Bioengineering (NIBIB)
National Institute of General Medical Sciences (NIGMS)

papers.title: MIMIC-IV, a freely accessible electronic health record dataset

modality.scope: Hospital and ICU admissions, including demographics, vital signs, labs, medications, notes.

ethics.legal_compliance: Compliant with HIPAA and MIT Institutional Review Board requirements.

known_limitations: Single-center origin limits geographic and institutional diversity.
Temporal shifts in coding, practice, and EHR systems may affect longitudinal consistency.
Demographic subgroup distributions (age, sex, ethnicity) not reported in source text.
Potential selection bias: only patients admitted to a tertiary academic medical center.
bias_and_limitations.modifications: De-identification applied; no synthetic data generation reported.
bias_and_limitations.representativeness_concerns: Not representative of global or even broader US populations; reflects one academic medical center.
bias_and_limitations.generalizability_statement: Results may not generalize beyond similar high-resource, academic, urban US hospitals.
bias_and_limitations.subgroup_coverage: No explicit reporting of subgroup coverage (e.g., race, gender, age bands).
bias_and_limitations.missing_data: EHR data inherently contains missingness due to clinical workflow variability; extent not quantified in abstract.

benchmarks: MIMIC-IV Benchmark (e.g., mortality prediction, sepsis detection)
tasks_and_use.excluded_tasks: Commercial deployment or direct clinical decision support without validation.

data_origin.selection_rationale: Patients admitted to the critical care units and the hospital of the Beth Israel Deaconess Medical Center.
data_origin.sampling_strategy: Consecutive admissions at a single academic medical center; no explicit random or stratified sampling described.
data_origin.aggregation_multisource: Data aggregated from multiple hospital information systems (EHR modules), but sourced from a single institution.
data_origin.data_shifts_overtime: Data collected across 2008–2022; known temporal shifts in clinical practice, coding standards (e.g., ICD-9 to ICD-10), and EHR software versions are expected but not quantified in source text.

population.target_population: Adult and pediatric patients admitted to hospital and ICU at Beth Israel Deaconess Medical Center.
population.inclusion_criteria: Hospital admission at Beth Israel Deaconess Medical Center.
population.missing_groups: No explicit statement on underrepresented groups; limited generalizability beyond single US academic medical center.

attribute_recording.unknown_proportion: Proportion of unknown/missing demographic values not reported in source text.

annotation.annotation_method: Derived from structured and unstructured EHR fields (e.g., ICD codes, lab results, clinician notes).

annotators.qualifications: Clinicians and coders at Beth Israel Deaconess Medical Center.

annotation.labeling_provenance: Labels derived from clinical documentation and billing codes; subject to real-world EHR noise and incompleteness.
annotation.label_noise_description: Inherent noise due to documentation practices, coding delays, and incomplete data entry in clinical settings.
